_about: Photogrammetry-style (AI) models of San Francisco landmarks: their source files and what tools/modelpack/pack.ts needs to make game-ready LODs of them. Intrinsic facts only (real size, which axis is the front, waterline, material); where a project puts one is that project's business (cityengine: public/landmarks/san-francisco-statues.json).

_fields.id: asset id in the assetkit-models-sf index
_fields.material: 'textured' (the file carries its own texture), else a shader for an untextured model: bronze (the default), copperoxide, concrete, whitestone, silver… (a material named in the file name wins)
_fields.front: the model's own axis its front faces, as the glTF loader leaves it: +z | -z | +x | -x
_fields.scale: { axis: x|y|z, metres }: the real size along that model axis; the whole model is scaled uniformly from it (a ship by its length, a statue by its height)
_fields.draft: ships: metres from the model's lowest point up to the waterline, after scaling
_fields.plinth: statues whose model has no base: the pedestal a renderer must draw, [width, depth, height] metres; absent when the model brings its own or stands on the ground
_fields.lods: levels to make: ratio of triangles kept (1 = all), texture cap in px, and the simplifier's error limit (fraction of the model's size; default 0.02 — a far LOD of a rigged ship needs more, or the thin lines stop it)

models.name: Balclutha (1886 full-rigged ship)
models.description: Steel-hulled three-masted full-rigged ship built 1886 by Charles Connell & Co., Glasgow; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: Model length (z, 1.0 unit) runs from the bowsprit tip to the stern: 92 m overall (301 ft). The red bottom (antifouling) is about 8% of the length, so the waterline sits ~7 m above the model's lowest point; measured from the four-view render, 2026-10-18. Mast tops then stand ~49 m over the water (published ~44 m). Two LODs only: the simplifier stops at ~8 k triangles whatever the error limit (the rigging is hundreds of separate textured strips with UV seams), and most of the memory is the texture; beyond lod1's range a game draws its own stand-in (cityengine: the procedural ship).
